newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea sweet crudes buoyed by gas oil, sours weak.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea sweet crudes buoyed by gas oil, sours weak.

text.p: North Sea sweet crude rallied sharply on Thursday as gas oil stretched further into five-year high territory, traders said.
But sour crudes in the north and Mediterranean weakened relative to the other grades.
"The whole thing is being dictated by the high premiums for low sulphur gas oil," a crude trader at a European refiner said.

November Brent jumped 38 cents to $23.48 per barrel and Dated Brent increased its premium to November paper by 11 cents to +13 cents, for a 16-18 cargo. Another Dated cargo, loading on Oct 18-20, traded at November Brent +10 cents.

Local demand for most North Sea crudes was strong, while Brent found outlets in the United States and South Africa. The only Brent date to emerge from the chains on Thursday was kept by BP, dealers said.

Oseberg was the premium grade, having traded as high as Dated +43 on Wednesday, with Forties just behind at Dated +40 cents. But sour Flotta and Urals were relatively weak: a Flotta cargo traded at Dated -57.5 cents on Thursday, equivalent to 60 cents discount after late pricing.
In the Mediterranean, Urals slipped 10 cents to trade at Dated -70 cents cif Augusta on Wednesday.
There were plenty of other cargoes on offer, traders said.
A shipping inspector reported about 1.4 million tonnes due to load from the Black Sea by the end of next week.
Mediterranean sweet crudes, however, remained strong, with Algerian Saharan Blend offered at a 5-10 cent premium to OSP.
Some Nigerian crudes also benefited from the extraordinary strength of gas oil, dealers said, although trade was on hold pending confirmation of November loadings.
